note: update_helper is a developer tool for shipping configuration updates. It has NO admin UI (configure=null), no permissions, and stores NO config of its own. Two halves: (1) a drupal-code-generator generator run via 'drush generate update_helper:configuration-update' (aliases config-update / configuration-update) that diffs active vs a module's exported config and writes a CUD YAML to <module>/config/update/<name>.yml plus a hook_update_N in <module>.install; (2) the runtime service update_helper.updater (Drupal\update_helper\Updater, UpdaterInterface::executeUpdate($module,$name) returns bool, ->logger()->output() returns messages). Because it has no stored config, the medium (introspection) cases inspect its live CONTAINER footprint (service update_helper.updater => Updater; update_helper.config_differ => ReversibleConfigDiffer), verified live via drush php:eval get_class(). The hard (execution) cases have the agent write the correct code/CUD to a dedicated deletable scratch file under web/sites/default/ (update_helper_hook.eval.php, update_helper_cud.eval.yml) which the verify greps and the reset deletes -- no full cache rebuild is triggered (this shared site's 'drush cr' fatals in an unrelated canvas/ui_patterns collision). All facts grounded in update_helper.services.yml, src/Updater.php, src/UpdaterInterface.php, src/Drush/Generators/ConfigurationUpdateGenerator.php and templates/configuration_update_hook.php.twig.

evals.prompt: In a Drupal module I have a Configuration Update Definition generated by update_helper. Inside a hook_update_N(), how do I actually apply it and report the result? Which service and method do I call?
evals.expected_output: Get the update_helper.updater service and call executeUpdate($module, $update_name), then return $updater->logger()->output(). E.g. $updater = \Drupal::service('update_helper.updater'); $updater->executeUpdate('mymodule', 'mymodule_update_9001'); return $updater->logger()->output();

evals.prompt: How do I use the Drupal update_helper module to generate a configuration update (CUD) and its update hook? What Drush command do I run and where do the files end up?
evals.expected_output: Run 'drush generate update_helper:configuration-update' (aliases: config-update, configuration-update). It diffs active config against the module's exported config, writes the CUD to <module>/config/update/<update_name>.yml, adds a hook_update_N() to <module>.install, and exports the changed config YAML.

evals.prompt: What does a update_helper Configuration Update Definition (CUD) file look like, and what does update_helper do so it does not overwrite config that was already changed by hand?
evals.expected_output: A CUD is YAML with one key per config name, each holding expected_config (how the config must currently look) and update_actions (add/change/delete deltas), plus an optional __global_actions section (install_modules / install_themes / import_configs). The update is only applied when the live config still matches expected_config, so hand-edited or already-updated config is skipped (a warning is logged) rather than clobbered.

evals.prompt: On this running Drupal site, update_helper is enabled. Which service applies configuration update definitions from an update hook, and what PHP class does it resolve to? Inspect the live container.
evals.expected_output: Service id update_helper.updater, class Drupal\update_helper\Updater. Discoverable with: drush php:eval "echo get_class(\Drupal::service('update_helper.updater'));".

evals.prompt: update_helper computes a reversible diff between two configuration states. On this live site, inspect the container and tell me the service id it uses for that diff and the class behind it.
evals.expected_output: Service id update_helper.config_differ, class Drupal\update_helper\ReversibleConfigDiffer. Discoverable with: drush php:eval "echo get_class(\Drupal::service('update_helper.config_differ'));".

evals.prompt: Write a Drupal update hook that applies an update_helper Configuration Update Definition and returns the logged result. To avoid touching real module code on this shared site, write it into the scratch file web/sites/default/update_helper_hook.eval.php (create it). It must fetch the update_helper.updater service, call executeUpdate(), and return the update logger output.
evals.expected_output: The file defines a hook_update_N() that does $updater = \Drupal::service('update_helper.updater'); $updater->executeUpdate('<module>', '<update_name>'); return $updater->logger()->output();

evals.prompt: Write an update_helper Configuration Update Definition (CUD) that changes a piece of configuration. Without touching real module code, write it into the scratch file web/sites/default/update_helper_cud.eval.yml (create it). It must be in the CUD format update_helper.updater applies: keyed by the config name, with an expected_config section and an update_actions section.
evals.expected_output: A YAML file keyed by a config name (e.g. system.site) with an expected_config: block (current values) and an update_actions: block (e.g. change: with the new values).
